title: Cap. II Arg. 2: praescientia loci (Rom. 8:29–30 / 11:2 / 1 Pet. 1:2)
latin: Secundo, urgentur illa loca in quibus electio sive praedestinatio ad gloriam expressis verbis conjungitur cum praescientia. Ut Rom. viii. 29, 30. Quos praescivit, eos & praedestinavit ut conformes fiant imagini Filii sui, &c. Et Rom. xi. 2. Non repulit Deus plebem suam quam praescivit. Et 1. Pet. i. 2. Electis advenis secundum praescientiam Dei Patris in sanctificationem spiritus, &c. Ex hisce & hujusmodi locis inferunt adversarii, Deum eos ad gloriam elegisse, quos praescivit futuros conformes imagini Filii sui, id est, sanctos & bonos; ita ut haec praescientia futurae bonitatis sive sanctitatis fuerit causa electionis ad gloriam.
pass_a: Secondly, those places are urged in which election or predestination unto glory is joined in express words with foreknowledge. As Rom. viii. 29, 30. Whom he foreknew, them he also predestinated to be conformed to the image of his Son, &c. And Rom. xi. 2. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. And 1 Pet. i. 2. To the elect strangers according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, unto sanctification of the Spirit, &c. From these and the like places the adversaries infer that God elected unto glory those whom he foreknew would be conformed to the image of his Son, that is, holy and good; so that this foreknowledge of future goodness or holiness was the cause of election unto glory.
pass_b: Second: they press the places where election or predestination to glory is joined in so many words with foreknowledge — Rom. 8:29–30 ("Whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to his Son's image…"); Rom. 11:2 ("God has not cast off his people whom he foreknew"); 1 Pet. 1:2 ("elect strangers according to the Father's foreknowledge, unto sanctification of the Spirit…"). From these they infer that God elected to glory those he foreknew would be conformed to the Son's image — holy and good — so that foresight of future goodness or holiness was the cause of election to glory.

lemmas.gloss: whom he foreknew he also predestined
elect according to the Father's foreknowledge

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 2: foresight of sanctity not cause — decree precedes foresight
latin: In locis allegatis non dicitur Deus elegisse aut praedestinasse certos homines ad gloriam quia praescivit eos fore conformes imagini Christi, id est, sanctos & bonos, sed dicitur eos elegisse quos praescivit, atque praedestinasse ut conformes fierent, vel elegisse in sanctificationem. Praescientia igitur futurae sanctitatis non fuit causa praedestinationis, sed praedestinatio causa praevisae sanctitatis. Deus enim nullum bonum salutiferum & spirituale in hominibus praevidet, nisi quod ipse in illis operatur; nullum bonum operatur, nisi quod decrevit operari. Decretum igitur operandi gratiam & sanctitatem, quod in praedestinatione includitur, semper praecedit praevisionem gratiae & sanctitatis, quae hominibus inesse intelligitur.
pass_a: In the places alleged it is not said that God elected or predestinated certain men unto glory because he foresaw that they would be conformed to the image of Christ, that is, holy and good, but it is said that he elected those whom he foreknew, and predestinated them that they might be made conformed, or elected them unto sanctification. Therefore foreknowledge of future holiness was not the cause of predestination, but predestination the cause of the foresight of holiness. For God foresees no saving and spiritual good in men except what he himself works in them; he works no good except what he has decreed to work. Therefore the decree of working grace and holiness, which is included in predestination, always precedes the foresight of grace and holiness understood as present in men.
pass_b: Reply: those texts do not say God elected or predestined certain people to glory because he foresaw they would be conformed to Christ's image — holy and good. They say he elected those he foreknew, and predestined them to become conformed, or elected them unto sanctification. So foresight of future holiness was not the cause of predestination; predestination was the cause of the holiness foreseen. God foresees no saving spiritual good in people except what he himself works in them; he works none except what he decreed to work. The decree to work grace and holiness — already wrapped into predestination — always comes before any foresight of grace and holiness as in them.

lemmas.gloss: predestination causes the holiness foresight sees
decree to work grace precedes foresight

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 2: praescientia practica / scientia approbationis — Catharinus
latin: Sed ipsa verba expendamus paulo accuratius. Non dixit Apostolus, quos praevidit; sed, quos praescivit, οὓς προέγνω. At haec praescientia practica est, non intuitiva: & scientia approbationis vocatur a Theologis. Sensus igitur est; Quos Deus dilexit, & ab aeterno suo beneplacito secretos ab aliis comprobavit, hos praedestinavit, &c. Nihil usitatius in Scripturis quam ut scire sive cognoscere ponatur pro amare sive approbare; sicuti nescire pro odisse & improbare. Non novi vos, Matth. vii. 23. Novit Dominus viam justorum, Psal. i. 6. Hinc Catharinus in hunc ipsum locum, Quid est quod praescivit, nisi predilexit?
pass_a: But let us weigh the very words a little more carefully. The Apostle did not say, whom he foresaw; but, whom he foreknew, οὓς προέγνω. Now this foreknowledge is practical, not intuitive: and it is called by the theologians the knowledge of approbation. The sense therefore is: Whom God loved, and by his eternal good pleasure separated from others and approved, those he predestinated, &c. Nothing is more usual in the Scriptures than that to know or to cognize is put for to love or to approve; as not to know for to hate and to disapprove. I never knew you, Matt. vii. 23. The Lord knoweth the way of the righteous, Ps. i. 6. Hence Catharinus on this very place: What is that he foreknew, except that he foreloved?
pass_b: Weigh the words more closely. Paul did not say "whom he foresaw," but "whom he foreknew" (οὓς προέγνω). This foreknowledge is practical, not bare intuition — what theologians call the knowledge of approbation. Sense: those God loved and, by his eternal good pleasure, set apart from others and approved — those he predestined. Scripture often uses "know" for love or approval, and "not know" for hate or rejection ("I never knew you," Matt. 7:23; "The Lord knows the way of the righteous," Ps. 1:6). So Catharinus on this place: What is "he foreknew," if not "he foreloved"?

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 2: Vulgate "conformes fieri" — not election from foresight of works
latin: Secundo, non dixit Apostolus, quos praescivit futuros conformes praedestinavit; sed, quos praescivit (hoc est, predilexit) praedestinavit conformes fieri, ut vulgata versio recte supplevit, quod in Graeco contextu deest. Non itaque Deus praedestinare dicitur ex praescientia operum nostrorum, sed praescire bona nostra opera quae praedestinatis praeparavit.
pass_a: Secondly, the Apostle did not say, whom he foreknew would be conformed, he predestinated; but, whom he foreknew (that is, foreloved) he predestinated to be made conformed, as the Vulgate version has rightly supplied what is wanting in the Greek context. God therefore is not said to predestinate from the foreknowledge of our works, but to foreknow our good works which he prepared for the predestinated.
pass_b: Second: Paul did not write "whom he foreknew would be conformed, he predestined," but "whom he foreknew" (that is, foreloved) "he predestined to become conformed" — as the Vulgate rightly supplies what the Greek leaves open. So God is not said to predestine from foresight of our works, but to foreknow the good works he prepared for those already predestined.

lemmas.gloss: Vulgate supply: predestined to become conformed
foreknow works prepared for the predestined

title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 2 close: Augustine — works prepared in predestination (Eph. 2:10)
latin: Audiamus Augustinum; qui lib. 2. De bono persever. c. 14. praedestinationem definivit, Praescientia & praeparatio beneficiorum Dei quibus certissime liberantur quicunque liberantur. Et apertius, cap. 17. Quibuscunque Deus sacra dona donat, proculdubio donaturum se esse praescivit, & in sua praescientia praeparavit. Nam in sua praescientia opera sua futura disponere, id omnino, nec aliud quicquam, est praedestinare. Ex quibus verbis facile videtis quam dolose & impie agant, qui gratuitam praedestinationem praescientia operum conentur obscurare, cum Deus nulla in nobis bona opera praeviderit, nulli praesciverit fidem aut sanctitatem, nisi eam quam in ipso decreto praedestinationis nobis praeparavit. Non igitur exinde praedestinavit nos quod praevidit bona opera facturos; sed ex eo praevidit bona opera facturos, quia in praedestinatione nostra praeparata sunt nobis bona opera, ut in illis ambulemus; Ephes. ii. 10.
pass_a: Let us hear Augustine, who in book 2 On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 14, defined predestination as the foreknowledge and preparation of the benefits of God by which whosoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. And more openly, chapter 17: To whomsoever God gives his sacred gifts, without doubt he foresaw that he would give them, and in his foreknowledge prepared them. For to dispose his own future works in his foreknowledge is altogether, and nothing else, to predestinate. From which words you easily see how craftily and impiously they act who try to obscure free predestination by the foreknowledge of works, since God foresaw no good works in us, foresaw faith or holiness for none, except that which in the very decree of predestination he prepared for us. Therefore he did not predestinate us because he foresaw that we would do good works; but from this he foresaw that we would do good works, because in our predestination good works were prepared for us, that we should walk in them; Eph. ii. 10.
pass_b: Hear Augustine (On the Gift of Perseverance 2.14): predestination is the foreknowledge and preparation of God's benefits by which whoever is freed is most surely freed. More plainly still (ch. 17): to whom God gives his holy gifts, he without doubt foresaw he would give them, and in that foreknowledge prepared them — for to arrange his own future works in his foreknowledge is exactly, and nothing else, to predestine. So you see how craftily and wickedly they cloud free predestination with foresight of works: God foresaw no good works in us, foresaw faith or holiness for no one, except what he prepared for us in the decree of predestination itself. He did not predestine us because he foresaw we would do good works; he foresaw we would do them because in our predestination good works were prepared for us to walk in (Eph. 2:10).

lemmas.gloss: good works prepared that we should walk in them
free predestination not obscured by foresight of works
